dct_description_sm: At the northern tip of Herschel Island, RADARSAT-2 and ALSO-PALSAR imagery analyzed by Short et al. (2011) identified an area of approximately 0.3 km2 referred to as the Subsidence Bowl. Between August 2007 and September 2010, the area subsided more than 5 cm. This is an unexpected feature, as this plateau area is not predicted to have the same terrain movement as coastal slumps or riverbanks. Field validation was required to demonstrate that InSAR is an accurate and precise tool for monitoring the permafrost terrain of Canadas northern regions. Validation of the inSAR results have been compared to field testing conducted initially by Burn and Zhang (2009) and follow-up studies by Lantuit and Pollard (2008). This metadata file documents the ground-penetrating radar surveys carried out for the ground-truthing of this project.
dct_title_s: The application of ground-penetrating radar to ground-truth InSAR subsidence observations on Herschel Island, Yukon Territory
